# EvBreadcrumb

> Show the user's location within a hierarchy and let them navigate back to any ancestor level.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:breadcrumb` |
| Layer | Organism (`src/organisms`) |
| Import | `import { EvBreadcrumb } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvBreadcrumb>` or `<ev-breadcrumb>` |
| Source | `src/organisms/breadcrumb/EvBreadcrumb.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<nav class="ev-breadcrumb">` |

## Example

```vue
<EvBreadcrumb :items='[{"label":"Beranda","href":"#","icon":true},{"label":"Pengadaan","href":"#"},{"label":"Detail"}]' />
```

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Breadcrumb**, frame `4179:64595` (Breadcrumb). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use on pages nested two or more levels deep so users can see where they are and jump back to any parent section.

### When not to use

- Flat sites with a single level. As primary navigation — breadcrumbs complement, not replace, the main nav. For linear flows → use a Stepper.

### Do

- Show the full path from home to the current page. Make every level except the current one a link. Collapse long trails with an ellipsis.

### Don't

- Don't make the current page a link. Don't wrap the trail onto two lines — collapse with the ellipsis instead. Don't omit the home level.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvBreadcrumb`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<nav class="ev-breadcrumb">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:breadcrumb` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
